ingredients.item: ripe but firm tomatoes , cut into thick wedges
/2 sweet onion , sliced paper-thin, soaked 10 minutes in cold water
Black pepper; 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
scallion or a few chives , sliced

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: The dressing whisked — soy, honey, vinegar, sesame oil — and tasted: it should run lighter than the cabbage family's dressings (#F05), soy present but polite.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the spoon test: bright, mild-savory, the sesame forward. The tomato brings its own acid and sugar; the dressing frames it.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Wedges and onion folded in with spoons — one gentle turn, the tomatoes bruise at the second — pepper, sesame, scallion over.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the eating test: the wedge's cold burst, the onion's sweet crunch, the dressing's savory line through it. Beside jumulleok (#M06) — plain seared beef — this bowl is the plate's entire garnish department, and it is enough.

visualDonenessCues: the spoon test: bright, mild-savory, the sesame forward. The tomato brings its own acid and sugar; the dressing frames it.

the eating test: the wedge's cold burst, the onion's sweet crunch, the dressing's savory line through it. Beside jumulleok (#M06) — plain seared beef — this bowl is the plate's entire garnish department, and it is enough.
storageNotes: Eats within 2 hours; the dressed tomato keeps nothing. Dressing keeps a week.
Variations: cucumber wedges alongside the tomato; a few drops of yuja (#F05's jar) for the citrus fork; the same dressing over cold blanched green beans carries the method into autumn.
